channel.title: The AI Infrastructure Reality Check on Archit Singh
channel.description: Recent content in The AI Infrastructure Reality Check on Archit Singh

item.title: How AI demand puts upward pressure on DDR5 prices
item.description: Follow two routes from AI infrastructure orders to PC memory costs, then see where the evidence stops.

item.title: There isn't one AI bubble. There are six different businesses.
item.description: Follow the invoices from DRAM fabs to paying AI users to see who earns revenue and who carries the risk.

item.title: The GPU break-even equation nobody shows you
item.description: A per-GPU model for the price and billable hours needed to recover hardware, power, operations and the cost of capital.

item.title: The AI buildout is a critical-path problem
item.description: A deployment model shows why getting GPUs four months early can buy zero months of revenue and how to find the milestone that matters.

item.title: Five predictions that could falsify my AI boom thesis
item.description: Five public indicators with deadlines, baseline values and rules for scoring a miss.

item.title: What a sold-out HBM order book tells you
item.description: Follow a memory contract through deposits, shipment, deployment, and the economics of the application it ultimately serves.

item.title: What the AI buildout changes for a PC builder
item.description: A matched DDR5 kit shows why posted price and stock both matter, especially for a local AI workstation.

item.title: Why GPU rental and RAM prices can move in opposite directions
item.description: An AWS rate cut and a rising PC DRAM contract market show how installed capacity and fresh manufacturing respond to different constraints.

item.title: Where will the next AI infrastructure bottleneck move?
item.description: Track how scarcity can move from accelerator supply to power, networking, and customer demand using the throughput of one workload.

item.title: What happens when a GPU cluster hits a power limit?
item.description: Under the same site power cap, eight fast rack groups and twelve slower ones produce different queues. The better policy depends on the workload.

item.title: Will GPUs become obsolete before they pay for themselves?
item.description: A reproducible three- versus five-year cash-flow model shows why a working GPU can fall short of earning back its purchase price.

item.title: AI capex is climbing. What is happening to cash flow?
item.description: A filing-based comparison of Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta measures how much cash remained after equipment spending in the September quarters of 2025 and 2026.

item.title: The circular money flows behind AI infrastructure
item.description: Anthropic's AMD disclosure and CoreWeave's NVIDIA agreements show how hardware supply, equity and capacity commitments can point in opposite directions.

item.title: The true cost of serving one million AI tokens
item.description: Three public DeepSeek-R1 benchmark runs on the same rack show why a token cost estimate needs a latency target and an occupancy assumption.

item.title: AI demand, GPU utilization and profit are three different metrics
item.description: CoreWeave's Q3 2026 filing and a four-stage operating funnel show what each number can actually tell you.

item.title: The strongest evidence against the AI bubble narrative
item.description: Paid usage, measured business adoption and infrastructure consumption make the bullish case, with different limits.
